description: Curated FOC architecture hardening overrides. Generic derivation fills the rest.

ARCH-REQ-001.rationale: Top-level closed-loop motor control architecture. The source is an architecture specification, not a formal requirement baseline; the hardening pass makes it reviewable.
open_issues: Placeholder system parent ARCH-REQ-000; confirm the stakeholder/system requirement and ASIL allocation with the motor-control owner.

ARCH-REQ-004.statement: The architecture shall schedule CurrCtrl faster than SpdCtrl so that the inner current loop reacts before the outer speed loop changes IqRef.
ARCH-REQ-004.rationale: The scheduling relationship is a timing constraint; the source phrase 'because ... shall react' is made a single verifiable statement.

ARCH-REQ-010.rationale: Typed sender-receiver interfaces with units, ranges and computation methods are a data-dictionary constraint.
ARCH-REQ-010.constraint_rationale: Interface/data-dictionary constraint; verified by architecture review and DDS consistency check.

ARCH-REQ-020.statement: SpdCtrl shall convert speed error into a q-axis current reference using the specified speed-control algorithm with ramping, deadband, saturation and anti-windup.
ARCH-REQ-020.design_notes: PI control algorithm; gains, deadband, ramp rate and anti-windup limit are calibration parameters.
ARCH-REQ-020.constraint_rationale: The PI-control structure is retained as a deterministic control-design constraint; the gains are calibration parameters.

ARCH-REQ-025.rationale: Speed-controller gains, dead zone, ramp rate and anti-windup limit are exposed as calibration parameters.
ARCH-REQ-025.constraint_rationale: Calibration interface constraint; verified by calibration review and parameter-range test.

ARCH-REQ-030.statement: CurrCtrl shall convert d-axis and q-axis current errors into d-axis and q-axis voltage commands using the specified current-control algorithm with decoupling feedforward and voltage limiting.
ARCH-REQ-030.design_notes: PI current control with decoupling feedforward and voltage limiting; d/q gains and electrical parameters are calibration values.
ARCH-REQ-030.constraint_rationale: The current-control structure is retained as a deterministic control-design constraint; the gains are calibration parameters.

ARCH-REQ-036.rationale: d/q PI gains, electrical parameters, nominal DC voltage and voltage limit are exposed as calibration parameters.
ARCH-REQ-036.constraint_rationale: Calibration interface constraint; verified by calibration review and parameter-range test.

ARCH-REQ-047.rationale: Overcurrent, overtemperature, DC-bus, overspeed, nominal Iq and derating parameters are exposed as calibration parameters.
ARCH-REQ-047.constraint_rationale: Calibration interface constraint; verified by calibration review and parameter-range test.

ARCH-REQ-060.rationale: Verification constraint: component integration tests cover nominal run, startup, mode transition, current limit, overcurrent, overtemperature, DC-link fault and overspeed.

ARCH-REQ-061.rationale: Traceability constraint: each architecture requirement traces to MUD steps, runnable requirements, ports, calibration parameters and verification cases.

ARCH-REQ-005.statement: The architecture shall schedule electrical protection monitoring at 1 ms and thermal monitoring at 10 ms.
ARCH-REQ-005.rationale: Protection-monitoring periods are fixed at 1 ms and 10 ms.
